## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a family of probability laws on a common
discrete filtered measurable space and let $E=(E_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative
test supermartingale for $\mathcal P_0$
[[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]]. For every $P\in\mathcal P_0$ and
every $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
$$P\!\left(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge\frac1\alpha\right)\le\alpha.$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume AC. If $\mathcal P_0$ is empty the conclusion is vacuous;
otherwise fix $P\in\mathcal P_0$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and the nonnegative test
supermartingale $E$. All stopping times below use the discrete filtration and
time starts at zero.

[F1] [[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]]: under every null law $P$, $E$ is adapted, integrable, nonnegative almost surely at each time, a supermartingale, and $\mathbb E_P E_0\le1$.

[F2] [[def-discrete-stopping-time]]: $\tau$ is a stopping time when $\{\tau\le n\}\in\mathcal F_n$ for each $n$; a stopping time bounded by deterministic $N$ is bounded optional-sampling input.

[F3] [[thm-optional-sampling-for-bounded-stopping-times]]: under AC, for bounded stopping times and a supermartingale the expectation inequality points downward.

[F4] [[thm-continuity-from-below-for-measures]]: for an increasing sequence of measurable events, the measure of the union is the limit of their measures.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC supplies the conditional-expectation clauses used by the supermartingale definition and bounded optional-sampling theorem.

## Proof

1.1 Define $\tau=\inf\{t\ge0:E_t\ge1/\alpha\}$, with $\inf\varnothing=\infty$. For each $n$, $\{\tau\le n\}=\bigcup_{k=0}^n\{E_k\ge1/\alpha\}\in\mathcal F_n$ by adaptedness and the filtration property. Hence $\tau$ is a stopping time and $\tau\wedge N$ is bounded by $N$. [given, F1, F2, choose]

1.2 Apply F3 to the bounded stopping times $0\le\tau\wedge N$. For this fixed null law, $\mathbb E_P E_{\tau\wedge N}\le\mathbb E_P E_0\le1$. [F1, F3, A1]

2.1 On $\{\tau\le N\}$ the stopped value is at least $1/\alpha$, and on its complement it equals $E_N\ge0$ almost surely. Thus $\mathbb E_P E_{\tau\wedge N}\ge\alpha^{-1}P(\tau\le N)$; step 1.2 gives $P(\tau\le N)\le\alpha$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The events $\{\tau\le N\}$ increase to $\{\tau<\infty\}=\{\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge1/\alpha\}$. By continuity from below and step 2.1, the crossing probability is at most $\alpha$. Since $P$ was arbitrary, the bound holds under every null law. [F4, step 2.1] ∎

      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.08240

## Definition

Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a family of probability laws on a common discrete filtered
probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0})$. A process
$p=(p_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an **anytime-valid p-value process** for $\mathcal P_0$ if
each $p_t$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable with values in $[0,1]$ and, for every
$P\in\mathcal P_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
$$P(\exists t\ge0:p_t\le\alpha)\le\alpha.$$

At time $t$, the rejection rule at threshold $\alpha$ is the
$\mathcal F_t$-measurable test function $\varphi_{t,\alpha}
=\mathbf 1_{\{p_t\le\alpha\}}$ in the sense of
[[def-randomized-test]]. For any stopping time $\tau$, the event
$\{\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le\alpha\}$ is contained in the all-times crossing
event, so the definition controls rejection after data-dependent stopping.

    - title: "Aaditya Ramdas, Peter Grunwald, Vladimir Vovk and Glenn Shafer, Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference, §§2.5 and 2.7"
      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.01948

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $E=(E_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative test supermartingale
[[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]] for a null family $\mathcal P_0$.
Define
$$p_t=\begin{cases}1,&E_t=0,\\\min(1,1/E_t),&E_t>0.\end{cases}$$
Then $p=(p_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an anytime-valid p-value process for $\mathcal P_0$
[[def-anytime-valid-p-value-process]]. In particular, each fixed-time
$P(p_t\le u)$ is at most $u$ for $u\in[0,1]$, and every stopping-time rejection
event $\{\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le u\}$ is at most $u$ under every null law.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume AC. Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a null family, $E$ a nonnegative
test supermartingale for that family, and $p_t$ the process in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]]: under every $P\in\mathcal P_0$, each $E_t$ is a finite nonnegative measurable random variable.

[F2] [[def-anytime-valid-p-value-process]]: an adapted $[0,1]$-valued process is anytime-valid when every null law bounds its all-times crossing event by the threshold.

[F3] [[thm-villes-inequality]]: for every null law $P$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $P(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is the assumption used by the supermartingale conditional-expectation convention and Ville's bounded optional-sampling proof.

## Proof

1.1 The map $g:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ defined by $g(0)=1$ and $g(x)=\min(1,1/x)$ for $x>0$ is Borel measurable. Thus $p_t=g(E_t)$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable and $[0,1]$-valued. For $0<\alpha<1$, the threshold $1/\alpha>1$, so $p_t\le\alpha$ holds exactly when $E_t\ge1/\alpha$. [F1, given, construct]

2.1 Taking the union over all $t$ in the equivalence of step 1.1 and applying F3 gives $P(\exists t\ge0:p_t\le\alpha)=P(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_0$. This is the defining anytime-valid condition. [F2, F3, A1, step 1.1]

3.1 For a fixed $t$ and $0<u<1$, $\{p_t\le u\}\subseteq\{\exists s:p_s\le u\}$, so its probability is at most $u$ by step 2.1. Since $E_t$ is finite, $p_t>0$; hence the bound at $u=0$ is zero, and at $u=1$ it is trivial. For any stopping time $\tau$, $\{\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le u\}=\bigcup_{t\ge0}(\{\tau=t\}\cap\{p_t\le u\})$ is contained in the all-times crossing event for $0<u<1$; the endpoints follow as above. Thus fixed-time and stopping-time validity both hold. [F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $E=(E_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative test supermartingale
[[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]] for a null family $\mathcal P_0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume AC. Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a null family, $E$ a nonnegative
test supermartingale for that family, and $p_t$ the process in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]]: under every $P\in\mathcal P_0$, each $E_t$ is a finite real-valued measurable random variable and is nonnegative almost surely.

[F2] [[def-anytime-valid-p-value-process]]: an adapted $[0,1]$-valued process is anytime-valid when every null law bounds its all-times crossing event by the threshold.

[F3] [[thm-villes-inequality]]: for every null law $P$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $P(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha$.

[F4] [[def-p-value]]: a measurable $[0,1]$-valued statistic is a valid p-value for a nonempty null when every null law satisfies $P(p\le u)\le u$ for all $u\in[0,1]$.

[F5] [[thm-p-value-superuniformity]]: a valid p-value gives a binary threshold test of level $u$ by rejecting at $p\le u$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is the assumption used by the supermartingale conditional-expectation convention and Ville's bounded optional-sampling proof.

## Proof

1.1 The map $g:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ defined by $g(x)=1$ for $x\le0$ and $g(x)=\min(1,1/x)$ for $x>0$ is Borel measurable. Thus $p_t=g(E_t)$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable and $[0,1]$-valued. For $0<\alpha<1$, the threshold $1/\alpha>1$, so $p_t\le\alpha$ holds exactly when $E_t\ge1/\alpha$. [F1, given, construct]

2.1 Taking the union over all $t$ in the equivalence of step 1.1 and applying F3 gives $P(\exists t\ge0:p_t\le\alpha)=P(\exists t\ge0:E_t\ge1/\alpha)\le P(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_0$. This is the defining anytime-valid condition. [F2, F3, A1, step 1.1]

3.1 For a fixed $t$ and $0<u<1$, $\{p_t\le u\}\subseteq\{\exists s:p_s\le u\}$, so its probability is at most $u$ by step 2.1. Since $E_t$ is finite, $p_t>0$; hence the bound at $u=0$ is zero, and at $u=1$ it is trivial. For any stopping time $\tau$, $\{\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le u\}=\bigcup_{t\ge0}(\{\tau=t\}\cap\{p_t\le u\})$ is contained in the all-times crossing event for $0<u<1$; the endpoints follow as above. Thus fixed-time and stopping-time validity both hold. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

3.2 If $\mathcal P_0$ is nonempty, regard its laws restricted to $\mathcal F_t$ as the fixed-time experiment. Measurability in step 1.1 and all endpoint bounds in step 3.1 make $p_t$ a valid p-value for this null family by F4. Hence F5 identifies $\mathbf 1_{\{p_t\le u\}}$ as a level-$u$ binary test for every $u\in[0,1]$. When the null family is empty all lawwise assertions are vacuous. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC and fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Let $\Theta$ be a parameter set,
$(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ a family of laws on a common discrete filtered
measurable space, and, for each $\theta\in\Theta$, let
$E^\theta=(E_t^\theta)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative test supermartingale for the
singleton null family $\{P_\theta\}$. Define
$$C_t(\omega)=\{\theta\in\Theta:E_t^\theta(\omega)<1/\alpha\}.$$
Then $(C_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a $(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence
[[def-confidence-sequence]].

No measurable structure on $\Theta$ or joint measurability across $\theta$ is
needed for this pointwise membership and coverage statement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume AC, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the parameter family, and the candidate
test-supermartingale $E^\theta$ for each $\theta$. If $\Theta$ is empty the
conclusion is vacuous; otherwise fix an arbitrary $\theta$ when proving its
coverage bound.

singleton null family $\{P_\theta\}$. Define
$$C_t(\omega)=\{\theta\in\Theta:E_t^\theta(\omega)<1/\alpha\}.$$
Then $(C_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a $(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence
[[def-confidence-sequence]].

No measurable structure on $\Theta$ or joint measurability across $\theta$ is
needed for this pointwise membership and coverage statement.
